USD.catalyst: The US dollar index is holding at 101.92 above its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages, supported by a 0.49% weekly composite advance even as it softened 0.11% on the day following a 29k nonfarm payroll miss. The weaker employment release knocked out market pricing for an October Federal Reserve rate increase, which had gained traction after the FOMC delivered a unanimous rate hike lifting its policy target to the 4.00%-4.25% range through year-end. Meanwhile, US Attorney General Blanche confirmed the Department of Justice is satisfied with the Federal Reserve Inspector General report and is not reopening a criminal probe into Chair Jerome Powell. Two-year US yield spreads widened 43 basis points in the euro's favor over five sessions as markets recalibrated policy odds ahead of the October 27-28 FOMC meeting.

GBP.catalyst: The British pound is demonstrating solid resilience across G10 peers, gaining 0.26% on the session and 0.61% over the past week as softer US inflation and payroll data softened dollar momentum. Despite recent upside, sterling sits below its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages against the dollar as traders navigate energy price pressures tied to Middle East tensions. The Bank of England has signaled expectations for inflation to pick up through the second half of 2026 due to higher oil costs, after headline inflation stood at 3.3% earlier in the year. Market participants are monitoring domestic growth indicators and central bank commentary to gauge whether persistent price pressures will prompt further Monetary Policy Committee tightening.

EUR.catalyst: The euro remains broadly depressed, down 0.72% on a one-week composite basis and trading at 1.1256 against the dollar below its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages. Sentiment continues to be dampened by French 2027 fiscal budget turmoil widening peripheral debt risk, alongside remarks from European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde that cooled expectations for an October interest rate hike. Although the Governing Council raised its three key interest rates by 25 basis points on September 10 citing persistent Middle East energy inflation, market pricing reflects just 9 basis points of tightening for October compared to 17 basis points for the Fed. With leveraged funds holding net short contracts of 58.8k, market attention turns to whether the ECB holds policy steady until its December meeting.

JPY.catalyst: The Japanese yen continues its strong performance among major currencies, up 1.04% on a one-week composite basis even as it eased 0.05% on the day. Support has been driven by hawkish Bank of Japan expectations following remarks by Policy Board member Hajime Takata regarding consecutive rate hikes, with Tokyo Tanshi data placing the odds of a 25 basis point hike to 1.25% at 97%. Domestic debate has also centered on former board member Takahide Kiuchi's assertion that Japan does not require excessive monetary easing, alongside proposals regarding idle funds. Against the dollar, the yen trades at 157.78, remaining above its 20-day moving average of 156.26 while holding beneath its 50-day and 200-day moving averages.

AUD.catalyst: The Australian dollar advanced 0.23% on the day to 0.6958 against the dollar, though it remains down 0.50% over the week and trades beneath its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages. The currency retains underlying carry support from the Reserve Bank of Australia’s cash rate of 4.35%, which provides a 70 basis point AONIA-over-SOFR premium, even after Governor Michele Bullock signaled the possibility of a pause. Swap markets maintain fair pricing of around 16 basis points in remaining RBA tightening by year-end, while domestic resilience is bolstered by central bank analysis indicating Australian mortgage holders retain substantial equity. Leveraged funds hold an extended net long position of 55.7k contracts, leaving the currency sensitive to broader commodity fluctuations ahead of the RBA's November policy review.

CAD.catalyst: The Canadian dollar underperformed its peers with a 0.42% daily decline and a 0.48% drop over the week, tracking beneath its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages against the US dollar at 1.4245. Macro headwinds intensified after Canada's S&P Global manufacturing PMI slipped to 51.5 in September from 53.0 previously, alongside ongoing sensitivity to trade and auto tariff developments. The retreat contrasts with institutional forecasts that anticipate approximately 100 basis points of Bank of Canada tightening by the end of 2027 to lift rates toward the upper boundary of its 2.25%-3.25% neutral range. With speculative leveraged accounts heavily net short 49.1k contracts, the loonie remains exposed to positioning unwinds ahead of upcoming Canadian employment and trade figures.

CHF.catalyst: The Swiss franc gained 0.10% on the day and 0.28% over the past week, finding steady demand amid global bond market volatility despite trading at 0.8285 against the dollar above its key moving averages. Domestic data showed Swiss headline CPI rising to 1.0% year-on-year, though core inflation remained subdued at 0.5%, keeping price pressures well within the Swiss National Bank’s target band of under 2%. The central bank, which conducts monetary policy reviews on a quarterly schedule, continues to balance domestic price stability against exchange rate shifts. Cross-currency levels computed by the SNB placed the franc at 0.9441 per euro and 1.0968 per British pound, leaving the currency sensitive to external growth shocks.

NZD.catalyst: The New Zealand dollar rose 0.14% on the day to 0.5616 against the dollar, recovering from multi-month lows following the soft US employment print, but remains down 0.35% on a one-week composite basis below its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages. Domestic sentiment was pressured by Westpac-McDermott Miller consumer confidence slipping to 97.6 as higher energy costs weighed on households, even as local inflation expectations moderated. Interest rate swap markets continue to price a strong 75% probability of a Reserve Bank of New Zealand rate hike to 3.00% at its October 28 meeting. Traders are closely tracking international commodity prices and the RBNZ's policy communications for confirmation of the prospective policy tightening.

NOK.catalyst: The Norwegian krone underperformed across the board, falling 0.12% on the session and 0.50% over the week, with the US dollar trading at 9.608 kroner above its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages. The krone continues to be burdened by downside volatility in crude markets and projections from the International Energy Agency pointing toward a global oil supply surplus of 3.815 million barrels per day. Norges Bank foreign exchange transactions and liquidity operations managed through the Scandinavian Cash Pool have maintained orderly domestic funding conditions despite persistent currency softness. Upcoming Norwegian foreign exchange purchase quotas and regional energy price movements remain the primary focus for market participants.

SEK.catalyst: The Swedish krona slipped 0.05% on the day and dropped 0.60% over the past week, with the dollar advancing to 10.032 kronor to sit above its 20-day, 50-day, and 200-day moving averages. Riksbank policy expectations remain anchored around the 1.75% policy rate, with policymakers highlighting that any impulse for policy adjustments would likely stem from international financial spillovers or sharp adjustments in global equity markets. Although shifting international rate expectations had previously offered marginal support, elevated correlation to risk sentiment and tech sector valuations has weighed on the krona. The currency remains bound by broader European growth trends and upcoming Swedish inflation prints scheduled for later this month.
